index 0000000000..62a1bdbb90
--- /dev/null
+++ b/web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+import {addDelegatedEventListener} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';
+
+let anchor: {tr: HTMLElement, side: string} | null = null;
+let selected: HTMLElement[] = [];
+
+function newLineNum(tr: Element): number {
+  return Number(tr.querySelector('td.lines-num-new')?.getAttribute('data-line-num') || 0);
+}
+
+/** the new-side rows from `a` to `b` in either order, or null when they aren't in one hunk */
+export function collectRangeRows(a: HTMLElement, b: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[] | null {
+  const [first, last] = a.compareDocumentPosition(b) &amp; Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING ? [b, a] : [a, b];
+  const rows: HTMLElement[] = [];
+  for (let tr: Element | null = first; tr; tr = tr.nextElementSibling) {
+    // a hunk header, or expanded context which belongs to no hunk
+    if (tr.classList.contains('tag-code') || tr.classList.contains('line-expanded')) return null;
+    if (newLineNum(tr)) rows.push(tr as HTMLElement); // skips removed lines and comment rows
+    if (tr === last) return rows;
+  }
+  return null; // `last` isn't after `first` in this file
+}
+
+function setSelected(rows: HTMLElement[]) {
+  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.remove('range-selected');
+  selected = rows;
+  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.add('range-selected');
+}
+
+/** the selected range, when `tr` is its last row and it has more than one line */
+export function getSelectedRange(tr: Element): {rows: HTMLElement[], start: number, end: number} | null {
+  if (selected.length &lt; 2 || selected.at(-1) !== tr) return null;
+  return {rows: selected, start: newLineNum(selected[0]), end: newLineNum(tr)};
+}
+
+function selectLine(td: HTMLElement, extend: boolean) {
+  const tr = td.closest('tr')!;
+  const side = td.classList.contains('lines-num-new') ? 'right' : 'left';
+  if (!extend || !anchor) {
+    anchor = {tr, side};
+    setSelected(side === 'right' ? [tr] : []);
+    return;
+  }
+  window.getSelection()?.removeAllRanges();
+  const rows = anchor.side === 'right' &amp;&amp; side === 'right' ? collectRangeRows(anchor.tr, tr) : null;
+  if (!rows) {
+    anchor = null;
+    setSelected([]);
+    showErrorToast(td.closest('[data-range-invalid]')!.getAttribute('data-range-invalid')!);
+    return;
+  }
+  setSelected(rows);
+}
+
+// click a line number to start a range, shift-click another to end it; Enter / Shift+Enter do the same from the keyboard
+export function initDiffRangeSelect() {
+  const selector = '[data-range-invalid] td.lines-num[data-line-num]:not([data-line-num=""])';
+  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'click', selector, (td, e: MouseEvent) =&gt; selectLine(td, e.shiftKey));
+  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'keydown', selector, (td, e: KeyboardEvent) =&gt; {
+    if (e.key !== 'Enter') return;
+    e.preventDefault();
+    selectLine(td, e.shiftKey);
+  });
+}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package files

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	git_model "gitea.dev/models/git"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	access_model "gitea.dev/models/perm/access"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	"gitea.dev/modules/gitrepo"
)

var (
	// ErrSuggestionNotApplicable means the comment has no suggestion that can be applied: not a new-side code comment
	// on this pull request, or not exactly one suggestion block (#156 AC7)
	ErrSuggestionNotApplicable = errors.New("the comment has no suggestion to apply")
	// ErrSuggestionPullClosed means the pull request is closed or merged, or has no head branch to commit to (#156 AC5)
	ErrSuggestionPullClosed = errors.New("the pull request is closed or its head branch is gone")
	// ErrSuggestionPermission means the doer cannot push to the head branch (#156 AC2)
	ErrSuggestionPermission = errors.New("the doer cannot push to the head branch")
	// ErrSuggestionHeadMoved means the head branch has new commits since the page was loaded (#156 AC4)
	ErrSuggestionHeadMoved = errors.New("the head branch has moved")
	// ErrSuggestionOutdated means the commented line no longer reads as it did when the suggestion was written (#156 AC3)
	ErrSuggestionOutdated = errors.New("the suggestion is outdated")
	// ErrSuggestionNoChange means applying the suggestion would leave the file as it is (#156 AC10)
	ErrSuggestionNoChange = errors.New("the suggestion makes no changes")
)

// ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch means branch protection stops the doer from pushing to the head branch (#156 AC6)
type ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch struct {
	Branch string
}

func (err ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("branch %q is protected", err.Branch)
}

// CanApplySuggestions checks what does not depend on the comment: the pull request is open, has a head branch
// (AGit pull requests have none) and the doer can push to it. It returns the head branch's commit ID.
func CanApplySuggestions(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest) (string, error) {
	if doer == nil {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPermission
	}
	if err := pr.LoadIssue(ctx); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if pr.HasMerged || pr.Issue.IsClosed || pr.Flow != issues_model.PullRequestFlowGithub {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed
	}
	if err := pr.LoadHeadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if pr.HeadRepo == nil {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed // the fork was deleted
	}
	if pr.HeadRepo.IsArchived {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPermission // nobody may push to an archived fork; the route only checks the base repo
	}
	headPerm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pr.HeadRepo, doer)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	// includes "Allow edits from maintainers" on fork pull requests
	if !issues_model.CanMaintainerWriteToBranch(ctx, headPerm, pr.HeadBranch, doer) {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPermission
	}
	headGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.HeadRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer closer.Close()
	headCommitID, err := headGitRepo.GetBranchCommitID(pr.HeadBranch)
	if git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
		return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed // the head branch was deleted
	}
	return headCommitID, err
}

// ApplySuggestion commits the comment's single suggestion to the pull request's head branch, replacing the
// commented line. expectedHeadSHA is the head commit the page showed; message may be empty for the default.
func ApplySuggestion(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, comment *issues_model.Comment, expectedHeadSHA, message string) error {
	original := comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()
	if comment.IssueID != pr.IssueID || !original.Has() {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}
	blocks := comment.SuggestionBlocks(ctx)
	if len(blocks) != 1 {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}
	// a pending review's comments are visible only to its reviewer (FetchCodeComments, the API), so for anyone
	// else the suggestion doesn't exist; applying it would publish a draft into the branch history
	if err := comment.LoadReview(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if comment.Review != nil &amp;&amp; comment.Review.Type == issues_model.ReviewTypePending &amp;&amp; (doer == nil || comment.Review.ReviewerID != doer.ID) {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}

	headCommitID, err := CanApplySuggestions(ctx, doer, pr)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if headCommitID != expectedHeadSHA {
		return ErrSuggestionHeadMoved
	}

	// the web editor's check, so the user gets our message rather than the pre-receive hook's output
	protectedBranch, err := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(ctx, pr.HeadRepo.ID, pr.HeadBranch)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if protectedBranch != nil {
		protectedBranch.Repo = pr.HeadRepo
		canPush := protectedBranch.CanUserPush(ctx, doer)
		if !canPush &amp;&amp; protectedBranch.UnprotectedFilePatterns != "" {
			canPush = protectedBranch.IsUnprotectedFile(protectedBranch.GetUnprotectedFilePatterns(), comment.TreePath)
		}
		if !canPush {
			return ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch{Branch: pr.HeadBranch}
		}
	}

	if comment.Invalidated {
		return ErrSuggestionOutdated // the page hides Apply on outdated comments, but a page loaded earlier may still post
	}

	headGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.HeadRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer closer.Close()
	headCommit, err := headGitRepo.GetCommit(headCommitID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	blob, err := headCommit.GetBlobByPath(comment.TreePath)
	if git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
		return ErrSuggestionOutdated // deleted or renamed since the review
	} else if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	content, err := blob.GetBlobContent(blob.Size())
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	newContent, err := applySuggestionToContent(content, int(comment.Line), comment.SuggestionContextLines(), original.Value(), blocks[0])
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := comment.LoadPoster(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err = ChangeRepoFiles(ctx, pr.HeadRepo, doer, &amp;ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
		LastCommitID: expectedHeadSHA,
		OldBranch:    pr.HeadBranch,
		NewBranch:    pr.HeadBranch,
		Message:      suggestionCommitMessage(comment, doer, message),
		Files: []*ChangeRepoFile{{
			Operation:     "update",
			TreePath:      comment.TreePath,
			FromTreePath:  comment.TreePath,
			ContentReader: strings.NewReader(newContent),
		}},
	})
	if IsErrCommitIDDoesNotMatch(err) {
		return ErrSuggestionHeadMoved // someone pushed between our check and the commit
	}
	return err
}

// suggestionCommitMessage is the doer's message, or the default, crediting the reviewer (#156 AC1).
// The comment's poster must be loaded.
func suggestionCommitMessage(comment *issues_model.Comment, doer *user_model.User, message string) string {
	if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
		message = comment.SuggestionCommitMessage()
	}
	// customer question 1 on #151 is open; the spec's default: the doer authors and commits, the reviewer is credited
	if comment.Poster.ID == doer.ID || comment.Poster.IsGhost() { // a deleted reviewer has no address to credit
		return message
	}
	sig := comment.Poster.NewGitSig()
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s\n\n%s: %s &lt;%s&gt;", strings.TrimRight(message, "\n"), git.CoAuthoredByTrailer, sig.Name, sig.Email)
}

// applySuggestionToContent replaces line lineNum (1-based) of content with the suggestion's lines, the way
// #154 draws the diff: "" deletes the line, "\n" leaves one blank line, otherwise one line per suggestion line.
// original is the line the suggestion was written against, and above the lines the reviewer saw right above it;
// content and both of those may use CRLF.
func applySuggestionToContent(content string, lineNum int, above []string, original, suggestion string) (string, error) {
	lines := strings.SplitAfter(content, "\n") // every element but the last keeps its "\n"
	if lines[len(lines)-1] == "" {
		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1] // content ended with a newline
	}
	idx := lineNum - 1
	if idx &lt; len(above) || idx &gt;= len(lines) { // also refuses lineNum &lt; 1, and a line that moved too near the top
		return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
	}
	// blame-based invalidation misses a line that moved onto an identical one, like another "}"; its neighbours don't
	for i, want := range above {
		if strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(lines[idx-len(above)+i], "\n"), "\r") != strings.TrimSuffix(want, "\r") {
			return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
		}
	}

	target := lines[idx]
	ending := ""
	switch {
	case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\r\n"):
		ending = "\r\n"
	case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\n"):
		ending = "\n"
	}
	if strings.TrimSuffix(target, ending) != strings.TrimSuffix(original, "\r") {
		return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
	}

	var replacement string
	if suggestion != "" {
		innerEnding := ending
		if innerEnding == "" { // the last line has no newline, so new lines in between take the file's own
			innerEnding = "\n"
			if strings.Contains(content, "\r\n") {
				innerEnding = "\r\n"
			}
		}
		newLines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(suggestion, "\n"), "\n")
		replacement = strings.Join(newLines, innerEnding) + ending
	}

	before := strings.Join(lines[:idx], "")
	if replacement == "" &amp;&amp; ending == "" &amp;&amp; idx &gt; 0 {
		// deleting a last line that has no newline: the line before it becomes last and loses its newline,
		// so the file still ends without one (#156 AC11)
		prev := lines[idx-1]
		before = strings.Join(lines[:idx-1], "") + strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(prev, "\n"), "\r")
	}
	result := before + replacement + strings.Join(lines[idx+1:], "")
	if result == content {
		return "", ErrSuggestionNoChange
	}
	return result, nil
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/markup/markdown"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// For a multi-line comment it returns every line of the range, joined by "\n".
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line &lt;= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	if c.RangeStartLine() &gt; 0 {
		lines, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
		if !ok {
			return optional.None[string]()
		}
		return optional.Some(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' &amp;&amp; last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

// RangeOriginalLines returns lines RangeStartLine..Line of a multi-line code comment as the
// reviewer saw them, false if the stored patch doesn't hold all of them.
func (c *Comment) RangeOriginalLines() ([]string, bool) {
	start := c.RangeStartLine()
	if start &lt;= 0 || c.Line &lt; start {
		return nil, false
	}
	return PatchLastNewLines(c.Patch, int(c.Line-start+1))
}

// PatchLastNewLines returns the last n new-side lines of a one-hunk patch, which end at the
// commented line, skipping removed lines. False if the hunk has fewer than n.
func PatchLastNewLines(patch string, n int) ([]string, bool) {
	rows := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(patch, "\n"), "\n")
	lines := make([]string, n)
	for i := len(rows) - 1; i &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; n &gt; 0; i-- {
		switch {
		case rows[i] == "" || rows[i][0] == '@':
			return nil, false // reached the hunk header
		case rows[i][0] == '+' || rows[i][0] == ' ':
			n--
			lines[n] = rows[i][1:]
		}
	}
	return lines, n == 0
}

// SuggestionContextLines returns the new-side lines the stored patch shows above the commented line, in file
// order. Applying a suggestion checks them too, since blame-based invalidation can miss the commented line
// moving onto an identical one, like another "}" (#156 AC3).
func (c *Comment) SuggestionContextLines() []string {
	if !c.SuggestionOriginalLine().Has() {
		return nil
	}
	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n"), "\n")
	hunkStart := -1
	for i, line := range lines {
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "@@") {
			hunkStart = i
		}
	}
	if hunkStart &lt; 0 {
		return nil
	}
	var above []string
	for _, line := range lines[hunkStart+1 : len(lines)-1] { // the last line is the commented one
		if line != "" &amp;&amp; (line[0] == ' ' || line[0] == '+') {
			above = append(above, line[1:])
		} // "-" is the old side, "\" is "No newline at end of file"
	}
	return above
}

// SuggestionBlocks returns the text of each ```suggestion block in the comment, found the way the
// rendered page finds them (#154 AC9). An empty block is "", one blank line is "\n".
func (c *Comment) SuggestionBlocks(ctx context.Context) []string {
	return markdown.FencedCodeBlocks(ctx, []byte(c.Content), "suggestion")
}

// SuggestionCommitMessage is the default message for committing the comment's suggestion (#156 AC1).
// The poster must be loaded.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionCommitMessage() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("Apply suggestion from @%s on %s", c.Poster.Name, c.TreePath)
}</result>
</event>

issue158:
Closes #158

## What changed

A reviewer can now comment on a range of new-side lines in Files changed. Click a line number, shift-click another in the same hunk, then click `+` on the last line of the range. The comment form and the posted thread are headed "Lines 18–22". "Suggest change" pre-fills every line of the range, and a suggestion renders with all the range's lines removed.

- **Storage:** the range start is `StartLine` in the comment's existing `CommentMetaData` JSON field. `Line` stays the range end, so thread placement, replies, the API and old rows are unchanged. No migration. `Comment.RangeStartLine()` and `Comment.RangeOriginalLines()` are the helpers S3/S6/S7 can use.
- **Server (`services/pull/review.go`):**
  - `CreateCodeComment` takes a `startLine`.
  - It checks that the range is on the new side and ends after it starts before it creates a pending review, so a refused range doesn't leave an empty review behind.
  - For a range it stores the hunk up to the range end and refuses (`ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid` → 400) a range that isn't in one hunk.
  - A reply inherits its thread's range.
- **Invalidation:** a range comment goes Outdated when the text of any line in its range changed at the new head (`checkRangeInvalidation`). The head commit is looked up once per push, and each file is read once, however many range comments it has. Single-line comments keep the existing blame check.
- **Frontend:**
  - `repo-diff-range.ts` handles click / shift-click on new-side line numbers, or Enter / Shift+Enter from the keyboard (PR diffs give those cells `tabindex="0"`). It refuses selections across hunks, expanded context or sides, with a toast.
  - The comment-form submit in `repo-diff.ts` now shows the server's error message when the POST fails, instead of failing silently. This can happen when a range was picked in a whitespace-ignored or single-commit view whose hunks differ from the full PR diff.
  - The `+` handler fetches the form with `start_line`/`line`, and the template renders the header.
  - S2's `initSuggestChangeButton` takes the range's lines.
  - S1's renderer splits the original on `\n`.

## Why

Reviewers could only suggest single-line changes. This covers #158 AC1–AC15. Apply-a-range was moved out of scope to S3 #156 / S6 #159 (see the spec discussion on the issue).

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: range header "Lines X–Y" on form and thread, saved for the range | `repo-diff-range.test.ts › collectRangeRows`, `› click then shift-click selects a range`; `TestCreateCodeCommentStartLine`; `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` (lines 3–5 stored); `TestCodeCommentRange/new_comment_form_shows_the_range`; `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC1_AC5_*`; `pr-suggest-change.test.ts › suggest a change across several lines` | unit, integration, E2E | AC; other (fixture repo1 git content) |
| AC2: upward selection gives the same range | `collectRangeRows` (reversed args); E2E (4 then shift-click 2) | unit, E2E | AC |
| AC3: one-line range is a single-line comment | `collectRangeRows` (same row); `repo-diff-range.test.ts › one line is not a range`; `TestCodeCommentRange/AC3_*`; `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC3_*` | unit, integration | AC |
| AC4: Suggest change pre-fills the range in order, indentation kept | `repo-diff-suggestion.test.ts › initSuggestChangeButton with a range`; `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` (stored lines in order); E2E | unit, E2E | AC; other (fixture repo1 git content) |
| AC5: range lines removed in order, block lines added | `suggestion.test.ts › a multi-line comment removes every line of its range`; `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLineRange`; `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC1_AC5_*`; E2E (3 removed, 2 added) | unit, integration, E2E | AC |
| AC6: empty block removes the range, adds nothing | `suggestion.test.ts › a multi-line comment removes every line of its range` (empty part) | unit | AC |
| AC7: changing any line in the range → Outdated | `TestRangeChanged` (first / middle / last); `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` (against `master`, where README.md ends at line 3); `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC7_AC13_*` | unit, integration | AC; other (fixture repo1 git content) |
| AC8: changing only lines after the range → not Outdated | `TestRangeChanged`; `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` (against `branch2`, unchanged); `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC8_*` | unit, integration | AC |
| AC9: range ending on the last line, last line or file deleted → Outdated | `TestRangeChanged` (last line deleted, file deleted, no final newline) | unit | AC |
| AC10: selection across a hunk header or expanded context refused | `repo-diff-range.test.ts › collectRangeRows refuses a range outside one hunk`, `› a range across sides or hunks is refused` | unit | AC |
| AC11: old side to new side refused with the message | `repo-diff-range.test.ts › a range across sides or hunks is refused`; E2E (closes the AC15 toast, then old 2, shift-click new 4 → a new toast, selection cleared) | unit, E2E | AC |
| AC12: direct POST with a bad range → 400, nothing saved | `TestCreateCodeCommentRange/AC12_*` (start = end, start &gt; end, old side, negative start, no new-side hunk; no comment and no empty pending review left); `TestCodeCommentRange/AC12_*` (400 with the message); `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC12_*` (start &gt; end, old side, two hunks, no hunk) | unit, integration | AC |
| AC13: single-line comments render and go Outdated as before | `TestPullReviewRangeComment/AC7_AC13_*` (single-line comment on line 2); existing `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine`, `TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute` unchanged and passing | unit, integration | AC, upstream behavior |
| AC14: Enter / Shift+Enter on line numbers selects a range | `repo-diff-range.test.ts › Enter and Shift+Enter select a range from the keyboard`; E2E (keyboard step) | unit, E2E | AC |
| AC15: a range refused at submit shows the message and keeps the form | `pr-suggest-change.test.ts › suggest a change across several lines` (bad start line submitted from the form) | E2E | AC |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** none; every AC has an automated test. The unit tests mock the toast, so the AC10 message text itself is only checked through AC11's E2E, which shows the same message.

**AI-written tests:** Claude Code wrote all new and changed tests:

- Go: `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLineRange` (including the "start after end" row), `TestRangeChanged`, `TestCreateCodeCommentRange`, `TestCreateCodeCommentStartLine`, `TestCodeCommentRange`, `TestPullReviewRangeComment`.
- Vitest: `repo-diff-range.test.ts` (including the click, keyboard and refusal tests), the range cases in `repo-diff-suggestion.test.ts` and `suggestion.test.ts`, and the array fix in `main`'s `initSuggestChangeButton in a form` test.
- E2E: `suggest a change across several lines`, including the keyboard selection, the refused-submit message and the AC11 step that closes the AC15 toast first.
- The `CreateCodeComment` call-site updates in `pull_review_test.go` and `api_pull_review_test.go`.

Expected values are the file contents and line numbers each test writes, or the fixture repo's actual git content (`git diff 4a35743 branch2`, `git show master:README.md`), read against the ACs, never copied from output. The integration test was also run with range invalidation disabled: the two range comments failed AC7 as expected, and the single-line comment still passed. The "no empty pending review" check in `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` was run against the old `review.go` and failed, then passed with the fix.

## CI / manual verification

- CI: all checks pass on the latest push. SonarQube Quality Gate passed with 81.5% coverage on new code.
- `go test ./models/issues/ ./services/pull/ ./routers/web/repo/`: pass.
- `go test -run 'TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute|TestAPIPullReview|TestPullReviewRangeComment' gitea.dev/tests/integration`: pass.
- `pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/repo-diff web_src/js/markup/suggestion`: 24 passed. `repo-diff-range.ts` line coverage is 97%.
- `pnpm exec vue-tsc`: clean after merging `main`.
- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/pr-suggest-change.test.ts --workers=1' make test-e2e`: 9 passed (3 tests × Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). With the default parallel workers, tests in this file hit their 10 s timeout locally, including the S2 tests this PR doesn't touch.
- `golangci-lint run` on the changed packages: 0 issues. `make lint-go` fails locally on a missing `modules/options/bindata.dat`, unrelated to this PR.

## Design

See the Design Decision and Decision 2 in #158. The start line is stored in `CommentMetaData` instead of a new column, and range invalidation compares text.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- A range comment stores the whole hunk up to the range end, not just the range plus `CodeCommentLines` of context. It's marked `shortcut:` in `createCodeComment`.
- The selection highlight stays after the comment is posted.
- The REST API can't create range comments yet (S7 #160).

**Encountered:**

- `checkInvalidation` still has its upstream `FIXME differentiate between previous and proposed line`. Ranges are new-side only, so I left it.
- The comment-form submit in `repo-diff.ts` didn't check the response status. Fixed here, since range refusals made the silent failure reachable.
- `CreateCodeComment` creates the pending review before `createCodeComment` can fail. This PR moved the range start/end check ahead of it, but a range that fails the one-hunk check still leaves an empty pending review, since that check needs the diff. Upstream, any other `createCodeComment` error does the same.
- `isErrBlameNotFoundOrNotEnoughLines` looks for `lines?` in git's message, but the local git prints `has only 6 lines`. So a comment past the end of a file returns an error instead of being treated as "not enough lines".
- `make lint-go` needs `bindata.dat` locally.
- `pr-suggest-change.test.ts` runs close to its 10 s per-test timeout, so it times out locally when run in parallel.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the spec revision, the implementation, all the tests listed above, the fix that moves the range check ahead of the pending review, and the test fix after merging `main`. spec:
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #154 (S1) and #155 (S2), both merged

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files changed tab of a pull request. She clicks the number of new-side line 18,
shift-clicks the number of line 22, then clicks `+` on line 22. The comment form is headed
"Lines 18–22". She clicks "Suggest change", and the block is pre-filled with those five lines. She
rewrites them as three lines and posts. Ben opens the PR and sees a "Suggested change" diff with
five red lines and three green ones. (Applying it is S3 #156.) A keyboard user does the same with
Enter on line 18's number and Shift+Enter on line 22's.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a reviewer clicks the number of new-side line 18 and shift-clicks the number of
  new-side line 22 in the same hunk, when they click `+` on line 22, then the comment form's header
  reads "Lines 18–22"; after posting, the comment's thread appears under line 22 with the header
  "Lines 18–22".
- [ ] AC2: Given a reviewer selects upward (clicks line 22, then shift-clicks line 18), when they
  click `+` on line 22, then the header reads "Lines 18–22" and the comment is saved for lines
  18–22, the same as AC1.
- [ ] AC3: Given a one-line selection (shift-clicking the line already selected, or clicking `+`
  with no selection), when the comment is posted, then it is an ordinary single-line comment with no
  "Lines" header.
- [ ] AC4: Given the comment form for lines 18–22, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then
  the inserted `suggestion` block contains lines 18 to 22 in order, with their indentation kept.
- [ ] AC5: Given a code comment on lines 18–22 whose body has one `suggestion` block of three lines,
  when it is shown in the Files changed or Conversation tab, then the "Suggested change" diff shows
  lines 18 to 22 as five removed (red) lines in order, followed by the three block lines as added
  (green) lines.
- [ ] AC6: Given a code comment on lines 18–22 with an empty `suggestion` block, when it is shown,
  then lines 18 to 22 show as removed and no line shows as added.
- [ ] AC7: Given a code comment on lines 18–22, when a push changes the text of any one line from 18
  to 22 (the first, one in the middle, or the last), then the comment is marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC8: Given a code comment on lines 18–22, when a push changes only lines after line 22, then
  the comment is not marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC9: Given a code comment on a range that ends on the file's last line, when a push deletes
  that last line, or deletes the file, then the comment is marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC10: Given a reviewer has selected a line, when they shift-click a line that would make the
  range cross a hunk header or include expanded context lines, then no range is selected and they
  see "A comment can only cover lines on one side of a single hunk."
- [ ] AC11: Given a reviewer has selected an old-side (deleted) line, when they shift-click a
  new-side line (or the other way round), then no range is selected and they see the same message
  as AC10.
- [ ] AC12: Given a direct POST to the code-comment endpoint whose start line is after its end line,
  is on the old side, or is not in the same hunk as the end line, when it is submitted, then the
  response is 400 with the AC10 message and no comment is saved.
- [ ] AC13: Given single-line code comments created before this change, when they are shown and when
  a push changes their line, then they render and are marked Outdated exactly as before.
- [ ] AC14: Given a keyboard user focuses the number of new-side line 18 and presses Enter, then
  focuses the number of line 22 and presses Shift+Enter, when they activate `+` on line 22, then the
  result is the same as AC1 ("Lines 18–22").
- [ ] AC15: Given a range the server refuses when the form is submitted (for example, one picked
  while the diff ignores whitespace or shows a single commit, so its hunks differ from the full PR
  diff), when the reviewer submits the comment form, then they see the AC10 message, the form stays
  open with their text, and no comment is saved.

### Out of Scope

- Ranges across files.
- Ranges on the old (deleted) side of the diff.
- Applying a range suggestion. S3 #156 (apply) and S6 #159 (apply several) read the stored start
  line to replace exactly the range.
- A start-line field in the REST API: S7 #160.
- Selecting by dragging; only click / shift-click, or Enter / Shift+Enter, on line numbers.
- Ranges that include expanded context lines (lines outside a hunk); they are refused (AC10).
- Following a range when lines are inserted above it. The comment goes Outdated, as single-line
  comments do today.

### Open Questions

- None. The maximum range length is resolved as the size of one hunk, with no separate cap; AC10
  and AC12 enforce it.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Store a range comment's start line as `StartLine` in the comment's existing
`CommentMetaData` JSON field (absent = single-line, as today), and keep `Line` as the range end.

**Alternatives Considered:**

- _A new `start_line` column on `comment`._ Typed and queryable, but needs a migration on Gitea's
  largest table, and the repo convention (`models/issues/comment.go`, `CommentMetaData`) is that
  non-index data goes in the metadata field. Nothing needs to filter by start line in SQL.
- _One linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4 #157.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so thread placement (`FetchCodeComments` keys on `Line`),
replies, the API and every existing row are untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads the
start line. Old rows have no `StartLine`, so AC13 holds without a migration.

**Consequences:** No migration. The start line can't be filtered in SQL. S3, S6 and S7 read it
through a helper (`Comment.RangeStartLine()`).

### Decision 2

**Decision:** Mark a range comment Outdated by comparing the text of lines start..end at the new
head with the range's lines stored in the comment's diff snippet. Single-line comments keep today's
blame check.

**Alternatives Considered:**

- _Blame every line in the range._ A comment stores one `CommitSHA`, so there is nothing to compare
  each line's blame against without a new per-line store.
- _Store the head SHA and diff the old head against the new head, mapping hunks onto the range._
  Handles lines moving, but needs a git diff per comment per push and much more code.

**Rationale:** It is the same rule S3 #156 AC3 uses for apply ("the line's text at head differs"),
so a range is Outdated exactly when its suggestion could no longer be applied.

**Consequences:** One file read per push for each file that has open range comments, shared by all
the range comments on it. A line rewritten to identical text is not flagged.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches the code-comment model helpers, the code-comment POST path (form, router, the patch snippet
and invalidation in `services/pull/review.go`), the diff page's JS and templates (range selection,
header, "Suggest change" prefill, keyboard selection, the comment form's error handling) and S1's
suggestion renderer: about fifteen files plus unit,
integration and E2E tests, with no new endpoint, table or migration.</result>
</event>

package files

import (
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

func TestZZRangeApplyProbe(t *testing.T) {
	c := &issues_model.Comment{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: 4, CommentMetaData: &issues_model.CommentMetaData{StartLine: 2},
		Patch: "diff --git a/f b/f\n--- a/f\n+++ b/f\n@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@\n a\n-x\n+b\n c\n d\n"}
	orig := c.SuggestionOriginalLine()
	t.Logf("original=%q has=%v ctx=%q", orig.ValueOrDefault(""), orig.Has(), c.SuggestionContextLines())
	_ = optional.None[string]
	out, err := applySuggestionToContent("a\nb\nc\nd\n", int(c.Line), c.SuggestionContextLines(), orig.Value(), "B\nC\nD\n")
	t.Logf("out=%q err=%v", out, err)
}

description: "Non-obvious commit/PR details beyond AGENTS.md: the model-ID trailer form, PR screenshots and how to host them."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 69cfac2d-d6c1-4099-8daf-14b2a01d3b02
  modified: 2026-11-04T22:43:33.694Z
---

AGENTS.md has the base rules: Conventional Commits, the `Assisted-by:` trailer only, approval for each commit, and the issue number in the subject. Beyond those:

- **Trailer form:** `Assisted-by: Claude Code:&lt;session model id&gt;`, for example `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`.
- **Editing a PR body:** `gh pr edit --body-file` replaces the whole body. Keep the `Closes #N` line and any image URLs.
- **Chores without an issue:** the team opens `chore/` PRs (e.g. #140, #142) with no issue, milestone, spec or issue number in the commit subject; they still need a teammate's approval. PR body section rules are in [[course-rules]].
- **No stacked PRs:** COURSE-WORKFLOW forbids basing a PR on another feature branch or merging one into another. For a dependent issue (#60 needs #57), build it locally on top of #57 without pushing; after #57 merges, rebase that unpushed work onto `main`, then push and open the PR.
- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch`** closes any PR based on the deleted branch instead of retargeting it (tested 2026-10-24). The course repo has `delete_branch_on_merge=false`.
- **Screenshots required:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` wants UI screenshots on PRs. Show "after" only for a new feature, and before and after otherwise.

Hosting screenshots:
- `gh` can't mint `github.com/user-attachments/...` URLs; only the web UI uploads there.
- Commit the images under `docs/sprint&lt;N&gt;/screenshots/` (since 2026-10-24). Not under `ai-logs/`: `.coderabbit.yaml`'s PR-description check fails any link into `ai-logs/`, screenshots included (it flagged PR #115; Sprint 1's #71/#74 predate the check).
- Reference them as `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/&lt;full-commit-sha&gt;/&lt;path&gt;?raw=1`. Use the SHA as pushed: an amend or squash before the push changes it, and the old link 404s. Pin the SHA, not the branch, so the images survive branch deletion.

Taking screenshots (done for PR #71):
- Use headless Chromium with `colorScheme: 'light' | 'dark'` and `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, then `page.screenshot` with a `clip`.
- Read each image back to check the crop.
- Rebuild first, or the footer shows a stale version.
- After pushing, confirm each `?raw=1` URL returns 200 as an image.

**Why:** The course fork diverges from default attribution, and these screenshot details each cost a retry.
**How to apply:** Use with [[verify-skill]] for the capture. Commit identity is in [[course-repo-and-identity]].

https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/149#issuecomment-6802369466
### Code Review — @controlled-opposition

**Checked:** Read the diff against #145's ACs. Pulled the branch and ran `TestCreateIssueDependency*` in `models/issues` and `TestWebAddIssueDependencyLoop`, `TestAPIAddIssueDependencyLoop` and `TestAPICreateIssueDependency*` in `tests/integration` (SQLite). All passed, and the integration tests finish in under 0.1s each. Then I swapped in `main`'s `dependency.go`, API handler and locale file and ran them again. LoopOfThree, SelfDependency, LoopPastFirstBatch, both web cases and all 8 API refusal and duplicate cases failed, as they should. The no-loop cases (SharedDependency, Shortcut, BesideOldLoop, NoLoop, NoLoopBlocks) and the model's LoopOfTwo, which `main` already refused, still passed. `./.claude-students/check.sh` passes and CI is green.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | 9 | The walk starts at the new dependency and follows the chain until it reaches the issue or runs out of issues to visit. A self-dependency is caught on the first step, which covers AC3 without a special case. The `seen` set means a loop saved before this fix can't make the walk run forever, and BesideOldLoop tests that. Putting `Unwrap` on the error and calling `APIErrorAuto` in the handler fixes both endpoints in one line. The check-then-insert race is pre-existing and listed in Tech Debt, which is fine for this scope. |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | 9 | Each AC has a refusal case and a no-loop case on both `/dependencies` and `/blocks`. Shortcut is a good one: it rules out a check that refuses any dependency that is already reachable. Every refusal also checks that nothing was written, which AC1–AC3 ask for. LoopPastFirstBatch covers the chunked query. |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | 9 | One row per AC. Status codes and the message match the issue word for word. The table says where AC4's "nothing added" check goes beyond the AC. I ran every test listed (see Checked). |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | 9 | `dependencyLoopExists` is small and its comments explain why. It reuses `container.Set`, `slices.Chunk` and `db.DefaultMaxInSize`. Optional: `issueDepExists` is now only used for the duplicate check, so a name that says that would read better, but it's fine as is. |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | 8 | The swagger docs for both endpoints are updated. The BREAKING section tells API clients what to do. Optional: `guide/models-issues.md` joins the unrelated "Add a column" sentence onto one line over the wrap width, and the new `APIErrorAuto` paragraph in `docs/services-context.md` has a line past the wrap width too. Undoing the first and rewrapping the second would keep the diff to this change. |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | 9 | The PR lists all 19 AI-written tests, explains how their expected values were checked against the ACs, and describes the manual checks on a local instance. |
| Overall — merge as-is? | 9 | Yes. Approve. The two doc notes are optional. |

AI assistance: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) read the diff, ran the tests on the branch and with `main`'s code put back, and drafted this comment. I checked the findings and scores before posting.

https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/150#issuecomment-6802530301
### Code Review — @controlled-opposition

**Checked:** Read the source diff and traced the merge-box flow against #143's merge check (`services/pull/check.go`). Ran `TestGetMergeBlockingDependencies`, `TestMergeBlockedByDependencies`, `TestPrepareMergeBox*` and `TestIssueViewSidebarDependencyStates` locally (all pass), plus `PullRequestMergeForm.test.ts` (2/2 pass). CI is green on `eadd547`, including test-e2e. I didn't click through a live instance.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | 9 | AC1–AC6 all hold. Moving the condition into `mergeBlockingDependencyCond()` is a good call: the merge box and the merge check now use the same query, so they can't disagree. Both use `IsDependenciesEnabled` too, which makes AC6 match the check. Hiding "Manually merged" from a viewer who can't merge now (Decision 2) avoids the "Manually merged (When checks succeed)" form. One optional question below about scheduled merges. |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | 9 | Covers the blocking and non-blocking cases, including conflicted PRs, branch protection and dependencies the viewer can't read. Each case is checked at the right level, and the e2e test checks that the merge button comes back once the dependency is closed. |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | 9 | One row per AC plus Decision 3. The sources are AC wording, the issue discussion and upstream behavior, never the code's own output. The AI-written tests are listed and say which values you decided yourself. Local runs are listed under Checked. |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | 8 | Clean, and it follows how the existing merge box is built. Optional nits below. |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | 9 | The comments explain why, and the `.claude-students` docs and their guide twins are updated together. Tech Debt is honest, including the second permission lookup. |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | 9 | Says clearly what Claude did and what you decided, and you kept each commit small so you could review it with its tests. |
| Overall — merge as-is? | 9 | Yes. Approving. |

**Optional (not blocking):**
1. **A scheduled merge after its dependency closes.** Decision 3 keeps the schedule. As far as I can tell, `services/automerge` only re-checks a scheduled merge on commit status and push events, so closing the last dependency won't set it off on its own. If that's right, a follow-up issue or a note under Tech Debt **Encountered** would help.
2. **Closed or merged PRs.** `prepareMergeBoxDependencies` still runs the query and the permission lookups for these, but `prepareMergeBoxInfoItems` returns before showing those items. An early `if prInfo.issue.IsClosed { return }` would skip that work.
3. **A duplicate count in `PullRequestMergeForm.vue`.** The new `hasAllowedMergeStyle` repeats what `mergeStyleAllowedCount` already counts. `v-if="mergeStyleAllowedCount &gt; 0"` would do the same job with one counter.

I've drafted a review below but haven't posted it. Nobody has reviewed PR #177 yet: the only reviews are from bots (Gitar approved, SonarQube passed, CodeRabbit skipped). CI is green on the latest commit (`1112532`).

I'd request changes, for two reasons:

1. **The Apply button fails on every range suggestion.** #156 (Apply) is already merged. The Apply check compares one line of the file with all the range's lines joined together, so they never match. I confirmed it with a throwaway unit test on an unchanged file: it returns `the suggestion is outdated`. The button still shows on range comments, so a reviewer who posts a range suggestion sees an "outdated" error when anyone clicks Apply.
2. **Jack's spec on issue #158 was overwritten.** On 11-17 Jack pasted an updated PR description into the issue body instead of the PR. The user story, ACs and both Design Decisions are now only in the edit history, and the PR body still has the older description.

Locally, the Go unit tests, Vitest (33/33) and `TestPullReviewRangeComment` plus `TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute` (SQLite) all pass. I didn't run E2E.

### Code Review — @controlled-opposition

**Checked:** I read the full diff against #158's AC1–AC15, using the spec from the issue's edit history (see Required 2). I pulled the branch and ran `go test ./models/issues/ ./services/pull/ ./routers/web/repo/`, Vitest on `repo-diff*` and `markup/suggestion` (33/33), and `TestPullReviewRangeComment` with `TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute` on SQLite. All passed. I also ran a throwaway test of `applySuggestionToContent` on a range comment (see Required 1). CI is green on `1112532`. I didn't run E2E or click through a live instance.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | 7 | AC1–AC15 hold. Keeping `Line` as the range end means thread placement, replies and old rows don't change. Checking the range before the pending review is created is a good catch. `PatchLastNewLines` stops at the hunk header, so the server refuses cross-hunk and no-hunk ranges by itself. The one problem is how this works with #156, which is already merged (Required 1). Fixing it would raise this to 9. |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | 9 | Each refusal case is tested at the level where it happens. `TestRangeChanged` covers first, middle and last line, a deleted last line, a deleted file and a missing final newline. Running the integration test with range invalidation turned off to show AC7 fails is good evidence. |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | 7 | The newer table (now in the issue body) has one row per AC, and its sources are the ACs and the fixture's git content. The table in the PR body is the older version and is missing `TestCreateCodeCommentRange`, `TestCodeCommentRange` and the new `repo-diff-range` tests. Moving the newer description into the PR (Required 2) would raise this to 9. |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | 8 | Small helpers and short comments that explain why. The `headFiles` cache keeps the per-push cost to one read per file. Two optional notes below. |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | 5 | The newer description is clear and its Tech Debt is honest, but it's on the wrong page and #158 has lost its spec (Required 2). Once the spec is restored, this goes to 9. |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | 9 | All AI-written tests are listed, along with how their expected values were checked, and the mutation-style check of AC7. |
| Overall — merge as-is? | 6 | Not yet. Requesting changes for the two required items; both are small. |

**Required:**

1. **Apply on a range suggestion always says "outdated".** `ApplySuggestion` (#156, merged) compares the single line at `comment.Line` with `SuggestionOriginalLine()`, which this PR changed to return the whole range joined by `\n`. Those can never be equal, so every range suggestion fails with `ErrSuggestionOutdated`, even when the file hasn't changed. I checked this with a unit test: range 2–4 on `a\nb\nc\nd\n` returns "the suggestion is outdated". The Apply button still shows because `comments.tmpl` and `conversation.tmpl` only check `.SuggestionOriginalLine.Has`. Since applying a range is out of scope, the smallest fix is to hide Apply on range comments (`(not .RangeStartLine)` in both templates) and have `ApplySuggestion` return `ErrSuggestionNotApplicable` when `RangeStartLine() > 0`. A test for that, plus a line under Tech Debt **Introduced** pointing to #159, would cover it.
2. **The #158 spec was replaced by the PR description.** The 11-17 edit to the issue body replaced the user story, AC1–AC15, Out of Scope and both Design Decisions with an updated PR description. Please put the 11-13 version of the spec back from the issue's edit history and move the newer description into this PR with `gh pr edit 177 --body-file …`. Graders read the ACs and the D3 design decision from the issue.

**Optional:**

1. If a thread already exists on the range's last line, clicking `+` there opens the reply form and drops the selected range without saying so. In a pending review, a direct POST of a range onto an existing single-line thread returns the "one side of a single hunk" message, which doesn't describe the real problem. A note under Tech Debt is enough.
2. `rangeChanged` splits the whole file on each call. That's fine for now, but if many range comments land on one big file, caching the split lines in `headFiles` instead of the raw content would avoid splitting it again for each comment.

_I used Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) to help read the diff and run the tests. I checked the findings and scores myself._

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #154 (S1) and #155 (S2), both merged

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files changed tab of a pull request. She clicks the number of new-side line 18,
shift-

&gt; ### Code Review — [@controlled-opposition](https://github.com/controlled-opposition)

The one problem is how this works with [#156](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/156), which is already merged (Required 1). Fixing it would raise this to 9.

prBodyHead:
Closes #158

## What changed

A reviewer can now comment on a range of new-side lines in Files changed. Click a line number, shift-click another in the same hunk, then click `+` on the last line of the range. The comment form and the posted thread are headed "Lines 18–22". "Suggest change" pre-fills every line of the range, and a suggestion renders with all the range's lines removed.

- **Storage:** the range start is `StartLine` in the comment's existing `CommentMetaData` JSON field. `Line` stays the range end, so thread placement, replies, the API and old rows are unchanged. No migration. `C</result>
</event>
